newsitem.title: CANADA: China committed to Hong Kong autonomy, Chan says.
newsitem.headline: China committed to Hong Kong autonomy, Chan says.

text.p: Hong Kong Chief Secretary Anson Chan said on Thursday that China is fully committed to granting Hong Kong a high degree of autonomy after Beijing takes control of the territory in July.
Chan, the territory's top civil servant, met Chinese Premier Li Peng and China's top policymaker on Hong Kong, Lu Ping, for the first time last week in Beijing.

Speaking to a Vancouver business group, Chan said the meeting made clear that China intends to live up to its promises. She accompanied Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa to the Beijing talks to discuss the handover.

"It is clear the Chinese leaders are fully committed to the faithful implementation of the late Deng Xiaoping's visionary concept of 'one country, two systems' and Hong Kong people ruling Hong Kong," Chan said.

"There is a clear appreciation that only in this way can Hong Kong best serve the interests of China -- in raising the living standards in China, enabling China to play an increasingly significant role in the economic and political currents of the world and in securing the peaceful reunification of Taiwan with China," Chan said.

Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, reverts to Chinese rule on July 1. China has promised Hong Kong a high level of autonomy under the "one country, two systems" policy devised by late paramount leader Deng Xiaoping and laid out in the territory's post-handover constitution.
After the handover, Chan will remain in her post and become Tung's second-in-command.

Before leaving Vancouver on Saturday, Chan is due to meet with business groups, members of the city's large Chinese community, local government officials and a junior Canadian minister of foreign affairs.

Her main message has been to reassure Canadian businesses that Hong Kong will remain a stable and hospitable place for foreign investors after July. She urged Canadians to maintain trade links and deal directly with Hong Kong in areas where it will have autonomy over its own affairs.
